PLANNING BOARD TO MAKE RECOMMENDATIONS: After conducting its investigation, preparing a map of the proposed redevelopment area, and conducting a public hearing at which all objections to the designation are heard and considered, the Planning Board shall make a recommendation to the Town as to whether the Town should designate all or part of the Study Area as an area in need of redevelopment. 6. SOMERVE Mastery AQRA shall refer to the ECFT stormwater model developed using the 2013 Western Sedimentary Stormwater Study to allow for a more detailed analysis of the project area. CMA will review and incorporate all of the recent improvements conducted by SWCD since the completion of the stormwater study. CWA will submit the work to the County, drainage basins further to allow for the more detailed analyses of the project area and to have by block basis. CWA will update the model to include the level of revisions and links to the stormwater model to reflect the revised basin boundaries with the project area. CWA will run the updated stormwater model to obtain peak flood flows, flood durations, peak discharges for the existing conditions within the project area. CWA will also use the stormwater model to assess the effectiveness of the various potential yield management alternatives. CMA will run updated stormwater model for various scenarios which will include multiple combinations of the potential system improvement alternatives. CWA will use the stormwater model to compare the effectiveness of each scenario in reducing the peak flood stage and flood duration throughout the project area while also estimating the impact on peak discharge into the stormwater canal. The model results for the various stormwater alternatives scenarios will be discussed in the Basis of Design Report. CWA shall complete this task within 60 calendar days from receipt of the Notice to Proceed (NTP) from the City. Task 1.2 Permit Verification Based on the regulatory requirements, the implementation of the proposed stormwater improvements within the project area will likely be contingent on providing sufficient storage volume for water quality treatment of stormwater runoff prior to discharge into the Western Canal and on limiting the peak discharges within the existing stormwater outfalls. CWA shall review, evaluate, and compare the permit restrictions on the various potential system improvement alternatives. CWA will validate the water quality volume that could be provided under each potential system improvement alternative for comparison with the minimum volume per regulatory requirements. CMA will compare each design alternative under each potential system improvement alternative with the maximum allowable discharge per regulatory requirements. CMA shall meet with SWCD and with South Florida Water Management District (SFWMD) to present the potential system improvement alternatives for this project and to confirm the permit requirements for each potential system improvement alternatives. Permit requirements for each system improvements scenario will be summarized in the Basis of Design Report for comparison purposes. CWA shall complete this task within 60 calendar days from the completion of the Notice to Proceed (NTP) from the City. Task 1.3 Document Review-Thermal CWA will review all available topographic survey, atlases, design drawings, and/or record drawings for existing utilities proposed in the project area to determine the configuration of existing conditions. CWA will also review all past maps for the project areas to confirm the presence of any new easements at the location of the existing stormwater outfalls throughout the neighborhood. If the available past maps for the neighborhood do not display any utility easement at these locations, additional title searches will be conducted to confirm the presence of existing utility easements at these locations. This scope is limited to title searches for up to 10 parcel locations. CWA will perform necessary site visits to the project area for verification purposes. CMA shall complete this task within 60 calendar days from the Notice to Proceed (NTP) from the City.
